publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Far infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy is a well-established technique for investigating the dielectric response functions of phonons and plasmons in bulk and low-dimensional semiconductors. The vibrational properties of binary solids like the III-V and II-VI compound semiconductors are described quite well by a simple linear chain model which leads to a good description of the optical and acoustic branches of the phonon dispersion curves. In the long wavelength limit the model can be further developed to describe the polariton coupling between the photons and the optical phonons. This coupling leads to the-well-known reststrahlen band of high reflectivity between the transverse optic phonon frequency, /spl omega//sub TO/, and the longitudinal optic phonon frequency, /spl omega//sub LO/. The interface modes discussed here occur in the region of /spl omega//sub LO/.

articleTitle: Experimental tomography setup for imaging of electrodynamic structure on millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A tomographic setup has been developed for the millimeter wave band. Tomography images of the object cross-section were reconstructed using the frequency range 135.54-136.5 GHz. The developed software is based on the first-order diffraction tomography formulation. The system combines the possibilities of tomographs operating in "on passage" and "measurement under surface" regimes. The use of both these approaches will allow to create the millimeter wave tomograph providing the image reconstruction of the object under investigation. The new reduction method of the surface contribution in an image of subsurface objects is proposed and considered. The essence of the method consists in using leaky waves of a transmission line of electromagnetic energy, when the line is located close to a surface, for illumination of subsurface objects. The suggested version of tomography is orientated towards applications in industry, medicine, detection/identification of abandoned objects and other fields.

articleTitle: Laser driven electron acceleration
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Issues pertaining to laser acceleration in vacuum, neutral gases and plasmas are discussed. For acceleration in vacuum the limitations due to electron slippage, laser diffraction, material damage and electron aperture effects are discussed. To achieve multi GeV electron energies in the laser wakefield accelerator (LWFA) it is necessary to propagate an intense laser pulse long distances in a plasma without disruption. It is shown that electron energies of /spl sim/GeV in a channel guided LWFA can be achieved by using short pulses where the forward Raman and modulation nonlinearities tend to cancel. Further energy gain can be achieved by tapering the plasma density to reduce electron dephasing.

articleTitle: Compact 94 GHz Gunn diode oscillator using an overmoded waveguide resonator
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A millimeter-wave oscillator which incorporates an overmoded-waveguide resonator with an array of TE/sub 10/-mode waveguides containing Gunn diodes, has been developed as a means for achieving highly efficient spatial power combining. An efficiency of about 74% and an output power of 0.2 W (CW) at 94 GHz, has been achieved with a 3/spl times/1 waveguide Gunn diode array with dimensions of 8.1/spl times/8.2/spl times/30 mm/sup 3/.

articleTitle: Development of far-infrared semiconductor detectors
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The recent developments of semiconductor Si, Ge and GaAs blocked impurity band detectors (BIBs), and Si and GaAs homojunction interfacial work-function internal photoemission (HIWIP) far-infrared (FIR) detectors in extending the wavelength coverage and improving the focal plane array (FPA) performance are reviewed. The advantages, current status, and potential limitations of these FIR detectors are also discussed.

articleTitle: A compact formulation of diffraction at biperiodic structures
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Diffraction of electromagnetic fields at dielectric objects with biperiodic structures can be modelled by a network consisting of multi-conductor transmission lines. For such a network, the wave equation with its propagation constants is derived.

articleTitle: Dual band infrared/visible quantum well detector and optically pumped intersubband laser
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Deals with a detector concept for the simultaneous detection of thermal infrared and visible (or near infrared) light. We use both interband and intersubband transition processes in a quantum well structure for the device operation. Experimental results on both InGaAs/InP and GaAs/AlGaAs structures demonstrate the validity of this concept. The idea of dual band operation of an InGaAs/InP quantum well infrared photodetector (QWIP) is straightforward. A usual QWIP structure with InGaAs wells and InP barriers is used for mid-infrared detection. The second part reports on results ofa newly developed optically pumped intersubband laser. Intersubband transition between confined states in quantum wells is a fully collective phenomenon displaying distinct many-body effects. These effects are seen in an optically pumped intersubband laser.

articleTitle: The technique of obtaining IR information for MODIS
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: MODIS is an instrument to satisfy the demand to get more information about the Earth. As part of the information from MODIS, infrared information is important and necessary. It can help us to detect polluted water-areas and so on. For infrared information, the sensitivity is the most impoitant index, which is decided by the detector noise and circuit noise. Methods to reduce the circuit noise level including disturbance are described.

articleTitle: A study on third harmonic gyrotron
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A systematic study on Ka band low-voltage third-harmonic gyrotron is presented in this paper. Two types of complex cavity structures with gradual and abrupt transitions are employed in the gyrotrons. A nonlinear theoretical investigation and numerical simulation for interaction between electron beam and RF fields in complex cavities are given. A diode magnetron injection electron gun utilized in the gyrotrons is simulated numerically. The Ka band third harmonic complex cavity gyrotrons with a permanent magnet system are designed and constructed. The experiments of these gyrotrons are in progress.

articleTitle: Recent development on terahertz spectroscopy and measurement with phase locked backward-wave oscillators
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Discusses a really fast frequency scanning option for millimeter and submillimeter-wave synthesizers which opens as a consequence new possibilities for precise microwave measurements. This becomes possible due to development of synthesized radio frequency source with a discreteness of 0.03 Hz and switching time of about 200 ns without phase jumps. The source is based on 0-50 MHz direct digital synthesizer microchip. Frequency modulation by sine, square-wave, triangle, saw-tooth and other desired functions with precisely known frequency deviation and period of modulation is possible. The signal from the source is used as a reference in a phase detector of BWO PLL so the tube output radiation frequency follows the law of the radio source frequency change. Fast frequency scan/modulation without phase jumps of phase-locked BWO is available now within 0.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Noise in quasioptical amplifier- and oscillator arrays
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In this paper a novel method for decreasing the noise-figure of a quasi-optical amplifier system is presented. The employed technique is explained and the technological advantages and disadvantages with respect to applications for MM-waves are evaluated. Finally, experimental results in the X-band are presented and conclusions for higher frequencies are drawn.

articleTitle: Terahertz radiation from LO phonon-plasmon coupling modes in InSb film
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In this work we present broadband coherent measurements of THz radiation from an InSb film using a PC antenna detector. Ultrashort laser pulses and tight focusing of the gate laser beam on the electrode gap of the antenna detector enabled us to extend the response bandwidth of the detector to 7 THz. By using this ultrabroadband PC antenna detector, we observed the THz radiation from LO phonon-plasmon oscillations in InSb film for the first time. It was found that the radiation power was comparable to that originating from the photo Dember field on the InSb film surface. This suggests that the LO phonon-plasmon oscillations can serve as an efficient source for THz radiation.

articleTitle: A 492 GHz submillimeter-wave receiver
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A 492 GHz submillimeter receiver was designed for application at the POrtable submillimeter telescope (POST). The receiver includes a Schottky diode mixer, a phase-locked Gunn oscillator at 82.3 GHz coupled with multipliers (/spl times/2/spl times/3), and low-noise amplifiers. In this paper, the system configuration and performance are introduced.

articleTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Presents the front cover and table of contents from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Index to authors
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Luminescence of Cr/sup 3+/ in the gahnite glass-ceramics
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The transparent glass-ceramics doped by Cr/sup 3+/ were prepared in the system of ZnO-B/sub 2/O/sub 3/-Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/-SiO/sub 2/. The absorption and emission spectra of Cr/sup 3+/ were measured and studied respectively. The absolute luminescence quantum efficiency of 0.378 and scattering coefficient of 0.03 cm/sup -1/ were obtained.

articleTitle: Precise dielectric measurement of BeO at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A Fabry-Perot open resonator is designed and constructed in order to measure the dielectric properties with low loss dielectric materials in the Ka-band (26-40 GHz) frequency band. A 3-D finite element electromagnetic code is used to simulate the TEM00q mode in the open resonator. Measurements are made by both the length variation method and frequency variation method. The measured permittivity and loss tangent of BeO (995) are 6.7 and 7e-4, respectively.

articleTitle: Progress in the development of relativistic gyroamplifiers for future linear colliders
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We present the design results for our second harmonic coaxial gyroklystron tubes, which are expected to produce /spl sim/80 MW of peak power at 17.14 GHz in 1 /spl mu/s pulses. The beam voltage and current are 470 kV and 540 A, respectively, and the applied magnetic field is about 0.5 T. The input cavity operates near the cyclotron frequency at 8.57 GHz; all other cavities operate near the second harmonic at 17.14 GHz. The expected interaction efficiency is 32-37% and the gain is 47-60 dB, for 3 and 4 cavity tubes, respectively.

articleTitle: The modern wide range millimeter-wave resonator spectrometer
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The new type of installation in the wide range of frequencies 45-200 GHz for the investigation of dielectric absorption, atmosphere including, is developed. Special attention is paid both to the investigation of ultralow absorption of radiation in the modern high-quality dielectrics, including thin films and to the atmosphere absorption, including the lines of oxygen and water absorption. It was found out that silicon and diamond output windows for the megawatt microwave gyrotrons have the essential absorption in thin, /spl Lt//spl lambda/, surface layer, leading to the additional absorption and surface discharges. Also it was found out that practically all the role film materials have the noted anisotropy of dielectric parameters, which also depends upon the producer.

articleTitle: Two-layer flexible dielectric waveguide in millimeter wave band
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The bending characteristics of a two-layer dielectric waveguide are examined in the millimeter wave band. The difference of permittivity between core and cladding dielectric layer and the ratio of core to cladding radius are optimized to reduce the radiation loss at bend.

articleTitle: Vibrational energy-spectra of protein molecules and non-thermal biological effect of infrared light
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The author seeks to find answers to the following questions. What are the biological and medical functions of infrared rays? What are the effective wavelength and frequency and strength? What is responsible for the infrared absorption in the living systems? Is the biological process a thermal effect or non-thermal effect? Finally, what is the relation between the processes and the medical functions of infrared rays?.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonance and cyclotron resonance of magnetic materials in millimeter and submillimeter wave region
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Microwave spectroscopy of magnetic materials is a powerful tool to investigate their properties from a microscopic point of view. Especially, frequencies in millimeter and submillimeter region give many advantages for this purpose, although it is technically difficult to use these frequencies for real experiments. The author has been working on ESR experiments and developing sub-mm wave ESR equipment by use of FIR laser since the 1970s. It has been shown that the method of sweeping the magnetic field at constant frequency is much better than the usual spectroscopic method by an interferometer in the far infrared region, which had been the only way to observe ESR at such a high frequency before such experiments. Now frequencies up to 7 THz and magnetic fields up to 40 T are available at temperatures down to 0.4 K in our laboratory by using FIR laser, BTWT, Gunn oscillators and vector network analyzer.

articleTitle: Resonant locking of gyrotron oscillations by wave reflection from fluctuating plasma
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Experiments at the stellarator L-2M show that even a small reflection from the plasma may result in an essential broadening of the gyrotron output spectrum. The effect is explained as the resonant locking of the gyrotron by the reflected wave fluctuations.

articleTitle: The problems in measuring the peak power of single pulses modulating the carrier wave
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The paper describes a method often used in measuring peak power of single pulses modulating the carrier wave. It involves calculating the output waveform of rectangular and Gaussian pulses through a detector and determining the amplitude difference between them. The results show that the method causes some errors in the theory.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of electron beam-wave interaction in a MPW with an ion-channel taken into account
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Analytical theory of electron beam-wave interaction along a waveguide filled with plasmas immersed in an axial magnetic field is presented in this paper. The effect of ion-channel is taken into consideration; numerical results show that the magnetic field and ion-channel have considerable influence on the characteristics of beam-wave interaction.

articleTitle: A new type of corrugated circular groove guide [mode matching analysis]
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A new type of corrugated circular groove guide is analyzed. While deriving a series of simultaneous equations basing on boundary conditions, we obtain the characteristic equation of this guide structure.

articleTitle: The numerical analyses of the strip loop resonance box cavity
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: This paper presents a square structure box cavity based on a closed strip loop and its numerical analysis. The analysis shows that this kind of cavity is suitable for multilayer filter and can be used in both microwave and millimeter wave bands under different exciting schemes. Also, double degenerative modes may be used in designs of filters for merge/or connect with microwave monolithic integrated circuits due to the square section of the cavity.

articleTitle: Neuronal responses by transcranial magnetic stimulation in cortex
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a technique increasingly used as a non-invasive diagnostic and experimental tool in electrophysiology. TMS has advantages over electrical stimulation in its ability to stimulate deep nerves and the brain without discomfort. This noninvasive stimulation of the nervous system also seems to offer new opportunities for the investigation of neuronal activity. In this paper, using a transcranial magnetic stimulation technique in combination with microelectrode recording in the cortex of the mongolian gerbil, evoked trains of complex spikes were studied. It was found that the spike rate and duration of the neuronal responses depended on the magnetic stimulus frequency. This suggests that transcranial magnetic stimulation is a useful technique for studying neuronal activities non-invasively.

articleTitle: Energy modulation of nonrelativistic electrons with infrared evanescent waves
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Optical evanescent waves which are induced on a metal microslit by illumination of a light have been utilized to modulate a low-energy electron beam at optical frequencies. Experiments performed at the wavelength of 10.6 /spl mu/m have shown that energy of electrons can be changed more than 10 eV for an electron beam with an initial energy of 80 keV by using a CO/sub 2/ laser beam with a peak power of 7 kW.

articleTitle: Slotted Ka-band second-harmonic peniotron with axis-encircling electrons
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A harmonic peniotron has been designed for high efficiency and relative immunity to mode competition from gyrotron interactions. The device employs a 70 kV, 3.5 A, axis-encircling electron beam. To ensure stability from competing gyrotron interactions, the peniotron operates in the lowest order mode of a slotted four-vane circuit, the π/2 mode. The 33 GHz, slotted second-harmonic peniotron is predicted to yield 125 kW with an electron efficiency of 58% and a device efficiency of 52%. The device is being constructed at UCD and will be driven by a recently developed Northrop Grumman cusp electron gun.

articleTitle: Ultra short high power microwave generation associated with short pulse laser
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: It is demonstrated that a short microwave pulse (/spl sim/6 ns) is generated from cw or long pulse microwave source (9 GHz) by the laser produced overdense plasma. The cw microwave propagating in the waveguide is sliced by laser produced plasma at two different points along the waveguide. The generated pulse duration is determined by the group velocity of the microwave in the waveguide and the length between two points. Furthermore, twice the power is generated by adding the two pulses by this mechanism. The results are in good agreement with theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: Signal properties and the optical parameter design of a laser radar
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The 3 dB contrast criterion is suggested based on the statistical properties of the back-scattered signal light. In case of heterodyne detection, the signal light speckle size is considered to be a key parameter in the matching between the signal light and the local oscillator (LO) light. Furthermore, the angular discrimination of a scanning imaging laser radar (lidar) is concluded to be 0.75/spl Theta/ for heterodyne detection and 0.67/spl Theta/ for direct detection, where /spl Theta/ is the probe beam divergence angle. Based on these analyses, the relationship among the optical paramerers of a lidar is summarized, which may help us to design the optical system properly.

articleTitle: A ferroelectric frequency-doubling material-potassium lithium niobate
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The ferroelectric potassium lithium niobate crystal has been the material expected hopeful to provide directly the doubling of the frequency of a semiconductor near-infrared CW-laser. Perfect crystals have been grown. The frequency-doubling properties have been studied using a CW Ti:sapphire laser at room temperature. The crystal showed good second harmonic generation properties.

articleTitle: Potential for increasing the power of free electron masers using novel 2D Bragg coaxial structures
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In this work the first successful measurements of a 2D Bragg coaxial mirror are presented. The results of experimental study of 2D Bragg structures as well as the results obtained from numerical calculations show that two dimensional distributed feedback can be used to obtain single mode excitation in a large diameter coaxial cavity. A joint experiment at the University of Strathclyde currently under progress aims to achieve single mode operation in a 37 GHz free electron maser (FEM) when driven by an oversized electron beam of diameter in excess of 10 wavelengths.

articleTitle: Nondestructive evaluation of delamination in IC packages by millimeter-waves
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A method to evaluate delamination in IC packages by millimeter-wave technique was studied. An open-ended coaxial line sensor was used as source and also as receiver of millimeter-wave signal that was transmitted into and reflected from the packages. The phase of the reflection coefficient causes a shift due to the presence of the delamination. The phase shift of the reflection coefficient in the cases of with and without delamination was proposed to be used to evaluate the delamination.

articleTitle: Broad-band fast detection in Nb HEBs
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Discusses design and test of a niobium superconducting edge hot-electron bolometer which operates from a standard 4K helium cryostat. It has a peak optical responsivity of 160 V/W and a minimum optical NEP of 4 pW.Hz/sup - 1/2 / with a detection time constant of 1.6 nanoseconds. The detector can be used throughout the millimetre, infrared and optical spectral regions. These performance figures should make the device very useful for free electron laser and pulsed field detection applications.

articleTitle: Measurement of dispersion characteristics of periodically loaded conducting posts in a rectangular waveguide [for gyro-TWT]
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The dispersion characteristics of periodically loaded conducting posts in a rectangular waveguide, which could be utilized as an interaction circuit of Gyro-TWT, have been measured. The measurement method using short metal plate can measure dispersion characteristics more simply and rapidly than the perturbation method. Various structures of periodically loaded conducting posts have been measured in the passband to investigate their dispersion characteristics. The measured results are compared with HFSS and show good agreement.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of the dominant mode in elliptical waveguide
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In this paper, the finite element method is first used to discuss the dominant mode in elliptical waveguides. The electrical field lines of the dominant TE mode as well as the magnetic field lines of the lowest TM mode are presented.

articleTitle: Cyclotron resonance and related physics
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Reviews magnetospectroscopy on solids for mm- to IR-waves and presents the latest results on spectroscopy in megagauss magnetic fields and infrared spectroscopy in destructive megagauss fields using explosive flux compression. Magnetotransmission results for HgSe and GaN are discussed.

articleTitle: Physics and considerations on millimetre-wave free electron lasers with low energy electron beams
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In the frame of the development of a millimetre-wave source for industrial applications, the European Network on Microwave Applications of Industrial Free Electron Laser aims at producing a working design of a broadband, compact and low-cost millimetre-wave source (10-100 GHz) of sufficient power (more than 1 kW, CW or average) so as to be able to aid industrial manufacturing. For the sake of compactness, low electron beam energies (of about 100 keV) and currents of a few A at most, are required. In order to select the best candidates a study has been performed on the principles and physics of low energy electron beam millimetre-wave sources. Although the gyrotron is a well established and highly efficient millimetre-wave source, we are considering alternative sources such as the Cherenkov FEL, Smith-Purcell based FELs, and undulator based FELs for more cost-effective and technological simpler devices in the kW power range.

articleTitle: Study on an unmagnetized plasma-loaded two-stage backward wave oscillator and free electron laser
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A free-electron laser pumped by electromagnetic wave (EM-FEL) is a type of laser that uses a high-power electromagnetic wave as a wiggler to generate short wavelength radiation. It has potential to produce higher frequency radiation with low energy electron beams than a free-electron laser with a magnetostatic wiggler. Y. Carmel et al. (1983) and G. G. Denisov et al. (1984), observed the EM-FEL radiation at millimeter wavebands with a relativistic backward-wave oscillator (RBWO) at 3 cm as the electromagnetic wiggler. Z. Liang (1995) reported the results of an electromagnetically pumped FEL with a separated FEL interaction region from the RBWO. A plasma-filled RBWO with a strong guiding magnetic field enhances the peak power over the vacuum case by a factor of up to 8, and the peak power of an EM-FEL with a frequency from 12 GHz to 26 GHz was measured in the experiment simultaneously. In this paper, we report the experimental and simulation results of an unmagnetized plasma-loaded BWO and free-electron laser.

articleTitle: Field emission characteristics of CVD diamond coated copper field emitters
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The polycrystalline diamond films were synthesized on a copper substrate by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition technique. The field emission characteristics and the electrical characteristics of contacts between metal and diamond film have investigated.

articleTitle: Nonlinear analysis of plasma-grating filled Cerenkov dielectric maser oscillator considering beam velocity spread
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A large-signal analysis is carried out in a plasma-grating filled Cerenkov dielectric oscillator with a relativistic electron beam considering initial velocity spread. The decrease in efficiency is compensated by plasma injection. Below a critical plasma density, the interaction efficiency increases as the plasma density increases.

articleTitle: Optimizing the construction relations of chiral slab via genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A novel method of optimizing the continuous variable constitutive relation of multi-layered chiral slab based on genetic algorithm was discussed in this paper. This method derived continuous variable constitutive relations automatically, then calculated the reflection coefficient by wave-splitting method. Furthermore the genetic algorithm was used to search the maximum absorbability of the chiral slab with certain thickness.

articleTitle: High power RF generation by relativistic beams in dielectric structures and its application to the advanced accelerators
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We have studied the interaction of a high current relativistic electron beam with dielectric loaded waveguides as a source of high power electromagnetic radiation. A unique high current photoinjector-based electron linac was used to generate the drive beam for these experiments. Travelling wave dielectric structures with luminal (v/sub phase/=c) frequencies of 7.8, 15 and 20 GHz were used. The rf power levels generated in these experiments were very large-up to 4-20 MW. This class of RF sources has been used for two beam acceleration studies for future linear collider research. With the newly improved RF photoinjector at the Argonne National Laboratory (ANL), we expect to generate up to 0.5 GW RF power in the range of 20-60 GHz with a pulse length of tens ns. With this soon to be available RF power source, we could test acceleration structures up to gradients of 1 GV/m.

articleTitle: Research peculiarities of electron flow forming in undulators with longitudinal magnet field
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Conditions of electron flow forming in focus axis symmetrical system and system of undulators (Motz type) with linear field component have been researched in this paper. Spontaneous radiation of electron flow with low kinetic energy which moves by curvilinear trajectory has been received.

articleTitle: Principles of holographic multi-element coupling at infrared and millimeter-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Holography offers a very general solution to almost all applications in which power has to be combined, split or converted, and signal paths have to be interconnected. Possible applications for infrared and optical wavelengths are the fibre-to-fibre and laser-to-fibre-coupling. Our objective is holographic millimeter and submillimeter solid-state power combining. Preliminary experimental results of a 65 GHz holographic power combiner are reported.

articleTitle: Research on hybrid device of Si microlens arrays with long focus and IR detector arrays
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A new method, named step simulation, is proposed to fabricate refractive 128/spl times/128 element Si microlens (MLS) arrays for hybrid integration with PtSi IR Focal Plane Arrays (FPAs). By the method, the focal length of rectangle-based multilevel Si MLS arrays is over 1 millimeter, much longer than typical focal length of MLS array fabricated by conventional binary optics Fresnel technique. Si MLS arrays and IR FPAs are coupled with infrared glue. The IR responsivity of the hybrid device is improved significantly.

articleTitle: Recent advances in theory and performance of millimeter-wave magnetrons
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Spatial-harmonic magnetrons with a cold secondary-emission cathode are candidates for pulsed high-power sources in the 3-mm and 2-mm wave frequency bands and even below. We have recently developed a nonlinear beam-field interaction model in order to optimise their performance and to study the frequency and power limits. Both simulated and experimental results promise excellent performance of such miniaturized tubes which have reached a mature state for radar applications in the 2-mm wave band.

articleTitle: Bose-Einstein condensation of phonons in atmospheric radiative transfer
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Summary form only given. The inadequacy of conventional molecular models in accounting for observations of real atmospheric radiative transfer in the infrared and millimetre wavelength regions has been discussed several times in earlier Conferences of this series. Explanations of why this happens were however generally unsatisfactory until the relevance of Frohlich's insights about the behaviour of pumped phonons in biosystems was recognized. New laboratory work in the X band microwave region will be described which gives strong support to the Frohlich concept by showing how a threshold of power level must be exceeded for the condensation mechanism to be effective. In some of these researches the pump power is exclusively in the microwave region. It is at first surprising that its atmospheric effects have not previously been recognized in a wavelength region which has been so intensively studied. The principal reason is that pumping gives rise to sharp lines from maser action which could easily be missed unless they were specifically being sought. There are also complications from long relaxation lines and saturation effects.

articleTitle: High sensitivity isotope concentration-ratio measurement CO/sub 2/ infrared laser system. II
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: For high sensitivity measurements of isotope concentration-ratios of trace-level gas mixture, particularly including carbon dioxide isotopes, we tested a /sup 12/CO/sub 2/-/sup 13/CO/sub 2/ composite laser system containing intracavity absorption cells. Sensitivity enhancement obtainable by the intracavity absorption cell configuration is examined theoretically. /sup 13/CO/sub 2/ in atmospheric air is readily detected and minimum detectable concentration by the present system was estimated to be 70 ppb.

articleTitle: A novel broadband transmission-type sensor
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A novel, very simple transmission-type sensor for measuring the dielectric constant, especially of high loss materials, is proposed. The response obtained for different reference liquids from a mode matching technique compares well with the measured scattering parameters in the frequency range from 100 MHz to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Chaos in microwave oscillators
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Chaos is one of the more interesting recent developments in the area of nonlinear dynamics. It is found that microwave oscillators, being highly nonlinear and rather complex, are prone to chaos. In general chaotic behaviour of a dynamical system is characterised by: 1) extreme sensitivity to initial boundary conditions; 2) apparent internal randomness, viz. a messy and continuous frequency spectrum; 3) fractal dimension of its attractor; and 4) positive sign Lyapunov exponents. Having investigated, as an example, two microwave oscillators, we have found that they have in common a physical mechanism, which is responsible for their nonlinear dynamical behaviours and chaos.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of knife-edge field emission cathode performance
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: One of the potential advantages of vacuum field emission arrays (FEA) is that the FEA can produce high frequency modulated electron beams at high current densities. A knife-edge field emission array (KEFEA) structure has been built. The KEFEA cathode array consists of many knife field emitters, each with its own self-aligned surrounding gate. The initial tests of the KEFEA cathodes have shown a threshold bias voltage of less than 50 V. In this paper, the KEFEA emission performance has been studied by simulating a unit cell structure using the particle-in-cell simulation code MAGIC.

articleTitle: Computation of infrared extinction of the brass aerosol
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Infrared aerosols have proved effective in infrared countermeasure, since they have the special ability to screen infrared energy and can thus obscure infrared reconnaissance and guiding device. It has been realized that the infrared extinction depends upon many factors such as aerosol material compositions, particle concentration and particle size distributions. Hence particle size of the obscurants must be carefully chosen when other factors have been given. In this paper we calculated the infrared extinction characteristics of the brass aerosol. Now that similar calculations based on the Lambert-Beer's Law had been carried out, we employed here a more generalized theory In the calculation, we assumed the distribution function of the particle size to be lognormal and the particle shape to be spherical. Results from both Lambert-Beer's Law and the generalized theory were given and compared.

articleTitle: Design of a quasi-optical system for conversion of TE/sub 0n/ mode outputs of a gyrotron into Gaussian beams
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Presents a novel design of a quasi-optical system for conversion of gyrotron outputs into gaussian beams. It consists of a quasi-optical antenna, four focusing mirrors and a filter which removes the side lobes of the beam. The system is capable of converting three TE/sub 0n/ mode outputs into Gaussian beams.

articleTitle: Effects of buffer gas on miniature optically pumped submillimeter wave laser
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The effect of buffer gas N/sub 2/ on miniature optically pumped NH/sub 3/ submillimeter wave (SMMW) cavity laser emission at 67.2 /spl mu/m was studied theoretically and experimentally. It has been found that: 1) N/sub 2/ had a positive effect on laser output at 67.2 /spl mu/m; 2) sharp absorption in laser spectrum under certain gas mixture pressures corresponded to the threshold of "bottleneck effect".

articleTitle: Double resonance and four wave mixing FEL studies of InAs/GaAs quantum dots and local modes in ionic crystals
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A brief review is given of lifetime and line broadening studies with the free electron laser at FOM-Rijnhuizen (FELIX), emphasising work on far infrared (FIR) modulated photoluminescence (PL) of bound-to-bound transitions in InAs/GaAs quantum dots and mid-infrared (MIR) four wave mixing experiments on localised modes of H/sup -/ ions in calcium fluoride crystals. We have made new far/near infrared double resonance measurements of self-assembled InAs/GaAs quantum dots. The FIR resonance is unambiguously associated with a bound-bound intraband transition in the neutral dots, and analysis of the FIR double resonance linewidth enables us to show that the inhomogeneous broadening of the PL cannot be attributed solely to size and composition fluctuation. In addition we have made time resolved studies of local modes in ionic crystals, where nonradiative decay plays an important role in the optical pumping cycle of laser gain media. We have made pump-probe studies of the local modes created upon the introduction of a light impurity, in particular the H/sup -/ ion, in CaF/sub 2/ in the spectral region 700 to 1200 cm/sup -1/. We have also measured the free induction decay of this mode using a noncollinear degenerate four wave mixing geometry. The observed coherent transient is striking in having large quantum beat modulations at negative time which are associated with vibrational ladder climbing.

articleTitle: Conceptual design study of a gyrotron with an axis encircling electron beam
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In this paper, we present results of numerical experiments performed as a part of a conceptual design study of a large orbit gyrotron (LOG) with an axis-encircling electron beam formed by a novel electron gun with permanent magnet system. The results of simulations indicate the feasibility of a compact LOG with low current and low accelerating voltage operating on TE/sub 41/ mode at fourth harmonic. The required magnetic field is produced by NdFeB permanent magnet and additional coils for fine tuning of the field strength at the gun and cavity regions.

articleTitle: Gyroresonanant acceleration of electrons, muons and protons
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Gyroresonant acceleration of charged particles is explored in light of much that has been learned about the interaction of electromagnetic radiation and electron beams during decades of development of gyro-amplifiers and gyro-oscillators, examples are shown for high-gradient acceleration of electrons, muons and protons.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of a hole-gap helical groove slow-wave structure
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The hole-gap helical groove slow-wave structure, as an all-metal slow-wave circuit, has advantages of good heat dissipation and large size, and thus is suitable for use in a MM-wave TWT. By means of an approximate field theory, the expressions of the dispersion equation of the hole-gap helical groove slow-wave structure is obtained in this paper. The influence of various circuit dimensions on the dispersion relation is discussed by numerical computation.

articleTitle: Development for millimeter-wave PHEMT mixer
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The analysis and optimizing design for PHEMT drain mixer circuit in Ka-band is given in this paper. The nonlinear equivalent circuit and its parameters are simulated and obtained from the small signal S-parameter and the DC measurements of the PHEMT device. The drain mixer circuit is designed with optimization, making use of the harmonic balance method and the conversion matrices method. The result shows that the mixer has conversion gain 4 dB at RF 27.4 GHz and LO 33.4 GHz/10 dBm.

articleTitle: Design consideration of high-power high-frequency magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: High-power and high-frequency magnetically insulated transmission line oscillator (MILO) was made a design consideration. In terms of the two-dimensional fully electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation, the output power of 1.5 GW at C-band and 200 MW at X-band in MILO have been obtained.

articleTitle: Application of high power microwave technologies and millimeter-wave diagnostic techniques in HT-7 superconducting tokamak
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The Institute of Plasma Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ASIPP) has made great efforts in the developments of high power microwave technologies for the purposes of plasma current driving and plasma heating, and also in the developments of millimeter-wave techniques for plasma diagnostics. In 1994, the HT-7 superconducting tokamak that is used for experiments of magnetically controlled high temperature plasmas was constructed in ASIPP. After the establishment of the machine, we have developed a megawatt grade of a microwave system for driving of the plasma current and a megawatt grade of a radio frequency (RF) wave system for the heating of plasma ions. We are just developing a 200 kW-level of millimeter wave system for the heating of plasma electrons. For the diagnostics of plasma properties, we have developed two millimeter-wave systems to detect the radiated millimeter-wave from the magnetically controlled plasmas and a multi-channel far-infrared interferometer system for the measurement of the plasma electron density profile.

articleTitle: On the negative-mass instability in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Space-charge effects, the so-called negative-mass instability (NMI), as the reason for electron energy spread arising in the region of the electron drift between the cathode and the cavity of a gyrotron are discussed. Theoretical calculations are compared with the results of the experiments performed at Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe.

articleTitle: Measurement, analysis and evaluation of electromagnetic environment and population exposure in some typical cities of China
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Measurement analysis and evaluation of contamination from electromagnetic (EM) waves are conducted in Xiamen, Zhangzhou, Xinxiang and some other typical cities. The predictive models of EM wave propagation in urban areas are tested using the measured field data. It is recommended that the generalized Okumura-Hate model can be applied to the evaluation of population exposure to radiation in cities.

articleTitle: Low-voltage sources of magnet-breaking radiation (MBR) on the free electron beam
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We consider the possibility of making short-wave range active device based on magnetic-breaking electron radiation moving in heterogeneous magnetic field. In many devices such as ubitron, laser on free electron beams etc. one of the main elements that form spiral electron flow is the magnetic focus system making the required field distribution at the interaction space. The focus system of these devices is periodical in vacuum constant magnets. Radiation is a result of electron movement in a cyclotron orbit. Radiation coherent properties are defined by the periodic electrodynamic system.

articleTitle: Review on space application of IR opto-electronics technology in China
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. This paper presents China's infrared opto-electronic techniques for space application. The two most important fields reviewed in this paper are the measurements on the flying attitude of satellite and Earth observation from a satellite. All of the Chinese satellites with the spin or 3-axes stability technique have used the infrared flying attitude instrument to measure the satellite attitude relative to the Earth. The infrared band of 14-16 /spl mu/m is adopted using an uncooled thermal sensitive resistance detector. The twinkling eyesight is 1.5/spl deg//spl times/1.5/spl deg/ with scanning rate of 1-5 cycle/second and attitude sensitivity of 0.15/spl deg/. The study on a high attitude resolution technique is underway. Up to now, 5 Earth observation satellites with onboard infrared remote sensing instruments have been launched. Three onboard infrared Earth observation instruments are still working in orbit. They are an infrared/visible spinning-scanning radiometer on the FY-2A geostationary meteorological satellite, a 10-channel scanning radiometer on FY-IC sun-synchronous orbit meteorological satellite and a multi-band scanning radiometer on China-Brazil-1 resources satellite. The optical and mechanical scanning structure is used for the image acquisition. HgCdTe infrared detectors are used for the short and thermal infrared channels, while the Si detector is used for the visible channel. The higher spectral resolution remote sensing technique for space application is being investigation in China.

articleTitle: Development of advanced millimeter-wave plasma diagnostics
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: This paper reports on the recent results of two types of millimeter-wave plasma diagnostics, reflectometry and imaging, applied to a tandem mirror plasma. The ultrafast-sweep broadband and ultrashort-pulse reflectometry provide reliable density profiles under the existence of density fluctuations. The combination of high performance system and advanced data analysis methods are necessary for automatic evaluation of density profiles. A millimeter-wave imaging array in the frequency range of 60-90 GHz has been successfully applied for measurements of line-density and electron cyclotron emission (ECE) profiles. It is being installed in Large Helical Device (LHD). In order to cover the frequency range of the second harmonic ECE on LHD (120-180 GHz), a new detector using MMIC technology has been designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: System performance and experiments with the 110 GHz microwave installation on the DIII-D tokamak
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Summary form only given. A powerful microwave system operating at the second harmonic of the electron cyclotron frequency has been commissioned on the DIII-D tokamak. Two Gycom gyrotrons each of which generates about 750 kW for 1-2 s pulses, and two CPI gyrotrons with diamond windows and rated at 0.9-1.0 MW for 10 s pulses are in service. Two additional CPI 1.0 MW gyrotrons are being installed and a third Gycom gyrotron is available as a spare. The launcher system on the tokamak low field side can be scanned poloidally in the tokamak upper half plane and the launchers on two of the transmission lines can also be scanned toroidally in both the co- and counter-current drive directions. The elliptical polarization of the injected rf beam is remotely controllable. Phase retrieval and correction using a two mirror relay was employed for the Gycom gyrotrons, which generate flattened rf beam profiles, and also for one of the CPI gyrotrons with a Gaussian beam. A single ellipsoidal mirror was used to couple one of the CPI Gaussian beams to the waveguides and the beam quality for this arrangement was excellent. The primary mission of the microwave system is to permit current profile control leading to the improved performance of advanced tokamak operation in quasi-steady state. Initial experiments on current drive both near and away from the tokamak axis and on transport have been performed. The system performance and initial experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Electronic structure engineering of MWIR emitters
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Applications of continuous-wave room-temperature semiconductor laser diodes emitting in the mid-infrared (MWIR) range of wavelengths (from 2-5 microns) will be extensive. The achievement of CW room-temperature operation of MWIR semiconductor lasers has proved to be elusive. Physical processes which degrade laser performance, such as Auger recombination (which increases the threshold current) and intersubband absorption (which increases the internal loss) increase rapidly with decreasing band gap in bulk semiconductors. Thus the threshold current at room temperature can be expected to be dominated by intrinsic Auger recombination processes. As a result, the active region performance cannot be improved simply by growing cleaner material - the material itself must be designed for better performance. Several strategies have been proposed to reduce Auger recombination and internal loss in MWIR materials through the design of superior heterostructure active regions (electronic structure engineering). These strategies include the use of strain and quantum confinement to improve the balancing between conduction and valence densities of states. This type of band-edge engineering was previously developed for near-IR laser active regions, and has proved successful in improving laser performance. A new level of electronic structure engineering is possible in the MWIR through the use of the InAs-GaInSb-AlAsSb material system. The band offsets in this material system exceed three times the MWIR energy gap, and thus allow extensive tailoring of heterostructure materials to reduce the availability of final states for intersubband absorption and Auger recombination.

articleTitle: Simulation studies of the proposed far-infrared FEL amplifier at ISIR, Osaka University
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Computer simulation studies are currently underway for the proposed FEL amplifier experiment to be carried out using the existing 38 MeV, L-band linac based FIR FEL system. This paper describes the time dependent and time independent simulation results using Genesis code. The dependence of FEL amplifier characteristics are investigated such as power spectrum and profile, frequency spectrum and FEL bunching parameter on parameters like beam current, input power and interaction length. The operating current regime and input seed laser powers required for optimum amplification are given.

articleTitle: Review of the gyrotron backward wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Theoretical modeling and experimental investigations of the gyrotron backward wave oscillator are reviewed with emphasis on its saturated behavior which contrasts sharply with that involved in a resonant structure.

articleTitle: Introduction to MEMSTIC
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: MEMSTIC is our chosen acronym for Multi-Element Multiple-Substrate Terahertz Integrated Circuit which denotes a novel circuit technology especially suited for the submillimeterwave frequency range. It is just under development by 4 institutes from 3 German Universities closely cooperating within a NSF activity. In this overview, the basic ideas of MEMSTIC will be outlined which will be illustrated by the subsequent 10 papers of this session dealing with devices and components which shall in future be integrated into a complete submillimeterwave transceiver.

articleTitle: Time division multiplexing antenna array using sum-difference analysis with single transmit/receive channel for automotive application
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A novel antenna array scheme is proposed where two sub-arrays, which partially share array elements, use one transmit/receive channel in different time slots. Virtual sum and difference beams are formed through digital signal processing, then multi-target range, bearing and velocity are obtained simultaneously. Compared with multi-channel antenna array (MAA) antenna, this array has smaller size and lower cost and smaller computation. Together with smart structure and simple signal processing, time division multiplexing antenna array using sum-difference analysis linear frequency modulated continuous wave (TDMSD LFMCW) systems will allow roadside detection, lane prediction, and the classification of objects, thus making possible the intelligent interpretation of traffic scenes.

articleTitle: Characteristics of flexible dielectric tube waveguide in millimeter wave band
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Flexible cylindrical dielectric tube waveguide in millimeter wave frequency is studied. Low transmission loss and bending loss can be obtained through an optimization of three parameters such as the thickness, the relative permittivity, and the inner radius of dielectric tube.

articleTitle: A new open resonator method for the measurement of dielectric permittivity and loss tangent of low absorbing materials at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: An open resonator system is constructed for the measurement of real and imaginary part of complex dielectric permittivity and the loss tangent of low absorbing materials at 60 GHz. A full cavity length variation technique was employed. The cavity length of the Fabry-Perot hemispherical open resonator was varied in small steps (20 nano meters) to record the resonance mode patterns for a number of modes. It is no longer necessary to have any expensive tunable frequency source as the fine frequency tunability is substituted with the cavity length variation in ultra fine steps. The cavity length variation method has an additional advantage since it provides less noise in the resonance interferogram as a function of the cavity length compared to the equivalent interferogram recorded as a function of fine frequency sweeping. The measurements are made on a number of fused silica and polymeric specimens and dielectric permittivity and loss tangent results are compared with other published results.

articleTitle: Analysis of the residual error after nonuniformity correction for infrared focal plane array
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A new method to calculate the residual error after nonuniformity correction (NUC) of infrared focal plane array (IRFPA) is deduced and a comparison with the past theories is performed based on a quantity of experimental data. The new method proved to be more effective. Some useful conclusions can also be deduced.

articleTitle: Low power tests on a TE/sub 28.8/-gyrotron mode converter system
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: For the ERCH system of the plasma fusion experiment W7-X in Greifswald, Germany, ten 140 GHz gyrotrons each giving 1 MW continuous output power are foreseen. They include a quasi-optical mode converter system to convert the field distribution of the resonator mode (TE/sub 28.8/) to a Gaussian like output beam. A cold test set-up of this system consisting of an advanced launcher and three beam forming mirrors was was built for low power measurements and for comparison with the design calculations.

articleTitle: Development of the step tunable 140/110 GHz 1 MW gyrotron for fusion
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Electron-cyclotron heating and current control in plasma set-ups require gyrotrons with a level of CW power up to 1 MW at frequencies 80-170 GHz and efficiency not less than 50%. The output window was the key factor that limited the achievable pulse duration in gyrotrons. The CVD diamond single disk window is capable of full 1 MW CW operation. Recent results generated interest in the use of frequency tunable gyrotrons for ECRH plasma experiments. In this paper we discuss the main problems of the step tunable gyrotron and present the design of a step tunable 110/140 GHz 1 MW gyrotron. The 80 kV, 40 A beam is produced by a magnetron injection gun (MIG) with an average perpendicular-to-parallel velocity ratio of 1.2 and a transversal velocity spread below 25%. The microwave circuit has a TE/sub 22.81/-TE/sub 19.61/ cavity, which operates at 140 GHz and 111.5 GHz respectively. Electron beam parameters were optimized for efficient generation of the modes. These modes were chosen from the condition of the gyrotron CVD window transparency at the operation frequencies. The highly efficient quasi-optical mode converter was elaborated for operation with two different cavity modes.

articleTitle: IR-magnetospectroscopy on mercury selenide in ultra high magnetic fields
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We report on magnetospectroscopy investigations on HgSe in the infrared wavelength range using very high pulsed magnetic fields. We have observed interband transitions as well as the cyclotron resonance (CR) of quasi free electrons. Transient effects in the resonance intensities are due to hysteresis effects in the spin dependent population and provide a novel tool for the determination of the spin-lattice relaxation time.

articleTitle: A quasi-optical concept of accelerating structures fed by mm-wave sources
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: As future electron-positron colliders are projected to operate at enhanced accelerating RF fields, the breakdown limitation makes it necessary to increase RF frequencies relative to those used in the present day accelerators. At the shortest microwave frequencies, high power electromagnetic flows can be canalized only with strongly oversized waveguides (in particular mirror lines) and controlled with quasi-optical components: wave beam combiners, phase and electrically controlled switches, passive and active pulse compressors. Particle acceleration structures should be fed with distributed wave flows and out-filter spurious modes.

articleTitle: Frequency multiplier grid arrays for satellite applications
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: In the millimeter wave (26-40 GHz) region, a combination of new technologies, such as MMIC amplifiers and equalizers together with miniature TWTs, have resulted in the millimeter wave power module (MMPM) which produces record power densities at low cost. These same advantages can be extended to higher frequencies by frequency multiplying the output of the MMPM using nonlinear solid state devices and quasi-optical power combining. The resulting high power millimeter wave sources are ideal for satellite applications. A quasi-optical frequency multiplier grid array consists of thousands of varactor devices and antennas on a single wafer. This approach is extremely attractive because of its low fabrication cost, small-size realization and graceful degradation qualities. The eventual goal of this research is a high power source using an MMPM to drive frequency multiplier grid arrays. This hybrid technology source will provide high levels of cw output power up to 200 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of LiNbO/sub 3/ optical modulators with a ridge structure
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Hybrid-mode analysis is carried out for coplanar waveguide applicable to Z-cut Ti: LiNbO/sub 3/ optical modulators with a ridge structure. The analysis is based on the integral equations. Generalized trial quantities are introduced as virtual adjustable sources in the equivalent representation of the structure. The microwave effective index, attenuation constant and characteristic impedance as functions of frequency are computed. The effect of thickness of the buffer layer on the microwave effective index is also investigated. The obtained results are compared with data furnished by the literature. A good accuracy is obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic effects on biological cells
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The basic effects of an electric field on a cell can be described by considering the cell to be a conductive body (the cytoplasm) surrounded by a dielectric layer (the surface membrane). When an electric field is applied to this cell, the resulting current causes accumulation of electrical charges at the cell membrane and consequently a voltage across the membrane. If the membrane voltage exceeds a critical value, structural changes in the surface membrane occur with transmembrane pore formation, a process known as electroporation. If the membrane voltage is not excessive and the duration of the pulse is limited, membrane poration can be reversible and the cell survives, an effect that is used for gene delivery into cells. Electric fields required for electroporation are one to ten kV/cm.

articleTitle: Operation of a fast-frequency-step-tunable 1 MW gyrotron with hybrid-magnet system
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A hybrid magnet-system for a 1 MW 140 GHz gyrotron was developed. Problems which occurred during the experiments are discussed. Experimental results of fast magnetic and electric frequency tuning with steps of more than 14 GHz per second are discussed.

articleTitle: Electron beam-cavity system of 170 GHz gyrotron for ITER
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The opportunity of using TE/sub 28.7/, TE/sub 31.8/ and TE/sub 25.10/ operating modes for a CW 170 GHz/1 MW gyrotron for ITER is assessed. Parameters are optimized to achieve maximum efficiency of the gyrotron with an acceptable ohmic load on the cavity. Results of an experimental investigation of short pulse prototypes of the TE/sub 28.7/ and TE/sub 25.10/ gyrotrons are presented. Mauimum output power 1.4 MW, efficiency 36%, and 65% with single-stage depressed collector were achieved.

articleTitle: Study on properties of urea and L-/spl alpha/-alanine didoped triglycine sulfate (UrLATGS) crystals
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: This paper discusses the properties of triglycine sulfate (TGS) crystals doped with urea and L-a-alanine. Pyroelectric coefficient and dielectric constants and Curie temperature are increased with these two additions. Infrared spectrum and dielectric loss of UrLATGS are measured. It is more suitable for infrared pyroelectric detectors than undoped TGS crystals.

articleTitle: Microwave measurements of the propagation characteristics in a multi-beam waveguide system
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The main heating method for the stellarator W7-X which is currently under construction is Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) at 140 GHz. To meet the physical and technical demands of the W7-X machine a 10 MW ECRH system with CW capabilities has been constructed. To test the performance of the system and to measure the beam propagation characteristics, a prototype system is currently under construction. In this paper we describe this system and present first RF measurements on beam propagation.

articleTitle: Frequency scaling of high power gyroklystron systems
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We present the results of our scaling studies of gyroklystron systems from Ku-band to W-band. Scaling laws are used to show that both the electron gun and the microwave circuit can be scaled over a wide frequency range with an output power that is proportional to the signal wavelength. Limitations to the scaling are discussed.

articleTitle: Progress on the 28 GHz, 200 kW gyroklystron amplifier experiment for plasma heating at KBSI
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A high power microwave-assisted plasma heating experiment is underway at KBSI. The plasma heating system consists of a 28 GHz, 200 kW gyroklystron amplifier, TE01 transmission lines with low loss mitre bends, and a quasi-optical mode launcher. The design of the 200 kW gyroklystron amplifier has been completed. An experimental tube for peak power demonstration is fabricated and currently under rf cold-tests.

articleTitle: Anisotropic perfectly matched layer absorbing boundary condition used for biaxial media
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We have extended the PML to the conditions for a biaxial medium and proved that such a medium is passive. We have also examined the basic performance of a conductor-backed PML versus incident angle. Furthermore, we have used an FDTD and an FEM algorithm simulation to demonstrate the effectiveness of a biaxial PML layer when used to terminate a parallel-plate waveguide loaded with biaxial dielectric. As an application, the proposed ABC was used to compute the reflection coefficient of layered uniaxial composite material. We found that the computing time and space region was reduced and obtained perfect agreement between an exact analytical method and FDTD algorithm. This permits the study of a much broader class of materials than was previously possible. A more detailed investigation of the effect of the PML parameters on its performance is needed in order to define guidelines for its practical use.

articleTitle: The temperature effect of infrared absorption of protein molecules in living systems
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Infrared rays with 1.1 to 3 /spl mu/m and 5 to 7 /spl mu/m of wavelength can be absorbed by protein molecules which can cause vibrations of amide-I in the amino acid residues. The vibrations of amide-I can result in intermolecular excitations (vibrons or excitons). The main peak of 1665 cm/sup -1/ in the infrared absorption corresponds just to the energy of the exciton. However, the vibrations of amide-I can also cause the deformation of the lattice around it. Then the non-linear interaction between the amides and amino acids could result in self-trapping of the amide-I vibrational quanta (vibrons) or solitons. The mechanism is as follows. Through such an intrinsically nonlinear interaction between them, an amide-I vibrational quantum as a source of phonons causes shifts in the average positions of the ground state of the vibrations of the lattice. These shifts (the lattice distortions) in turn react, through this nonlinear interaction, as a potential well to trap the amide-I vibrational quantum and prevent dispersion of the energy of the amide-I vibrational quantum via the dipole-dipole interaction which exists in neighbouring peptides with certain electric moments. The vibron-soliton occurred in such a case. It is a dynamic self-sustaining entity. The main properties of the soliton is that it can move over macroscopic distances retaining the wave shape, energy, momentum, and other quasiparticles with velocity v. The red shift of the main peak, 1665 cm/sup -1/, is caused by the self-trapping of the exciton or the soliton. Using the following vibron model we can give the red shift and exponential function dependence of the infrared absorption intensity on temperature.

articleTitle: IR cyclotron resonance of solid states in magnetic fields up to 700 tesla
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We report on the first successful IR-cyclotron resonance experiment in ultrahigh magnetic fields up to 700 T generated by explosive driven flux compression. The sample under investigation was an epitaxially grown p-type cubic GaN-layer, a material which has become worldwide the subject of extensive experimental and theoretical investigations because of its application in optoelectronic devices operating in the blue-to-violet wavelength range. Three distinct transmission minima at about 90 T, 270 T and 400 T-430 T with a resonance depth of a few percent only, are clearly resolved. The data in the lower field region correspond excellently to results derived previously from experiments in fields up to 275 T generated by use of the single-turn coil technique.

articleTitle: Phase characterization of gyrotron beams using the moment method
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: We present the formulation and results of the moment method applied to the determination of phase profiles of gyrotron microwave beams from known amplitudes. While traditional approaches to this problem employ an iterative error reduction algorithm, the moment method calculates a polynomial phasefront based on weighted moments of intensity measurements. The method is illustrated by the successful application to a 1 MW gyrotron beam.

articleTitle: Investigations of microwave pulse shortening in a high power coaxial gyrotron
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Experiments have been performed on a coaxial gyrotron driven by the Michigan Electron Long Beam Accelerator (MELBA) at parameters: V=-0.8 MV, I=1-10 kA, and pulselength=0.5-1 microsecond. Microwave pulse shortening has been investigated by spectroscopic plasma diagnostics to characterize plasma effects inside the operating gyrotron. Radio-frequency plasma processing has been applied to clean the inside of the gyrotron in order to reduce the deleterious effects of plasma on the microwave pulselength and energy. Results show that plasma cleaning can extend the microwave pulselength and increase the integrated microwave energy output by 15-245% in this gyrotron.

articleTitle: The calculation of back-scattering radar cross section of plasma spheres
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The scattering of EM waves from plasmas has attracted much attention. In this paper, we calculated the backscattering RCS of plasma spheres. Many factors can affect the RCS of the plasma, such as the EM wave frequency, the plasma electron density and the collision frequency. So we considered these factors in the calculation and carried out parametric studies. The results from the calculation may be helpful in giving us an overall understanding of the RCS of the plasma sphere.

articleTitle: A new sparse technique for singular integral equations in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A simple matrix composition technique, based on the concept of measured equation of invariance (MEI), is proposed to numerically thin the matrix from singular integral equations, such as method of moments (MoM). This technique is referred to as matrix decomposition by the MEI concept (MDMEI). Since sparse matrices have many advantages for saving storage and computing time for large-size problems, many efforts have been done to thin the full matrix generated by the MoM. In order to generate the sparse matrix with little additional work on any of a variety of existent MoM programs, the MDMEI method is proposed. In this paper, the MoM matrices for a variety of problems, such as electrostatic problems, wire antennas, and 2- and 3-D conducting object scattering can be easily thinned by MDMEI.

articleTitle: Of electromagnetic waves and the experimental study on bioeffects of transient electromagnetic fields on cells and its applications
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: Many hot problems of non-thermal effects of electromagnetic waves, such as the effects on human beings of low frequency electric fields and the mechanism of the interaction between the biology body and low-intensity electromagnetic fields, were discussed. Moreover, experimental studies of transient electromagnetic fields leading to cell membrane deformation were studied and its possible applications presented.

articleTitle: Investigations into the infrared extinction of artificial aerosols
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: The artificial aerosol is widely used in modern battlefields to protect potential targets and to conceal movement of personnel and material. In this paper we calculated the double-band infrared extinction coefficients of the aerosol and compared them with our experimental data. In the calculation, the particulates were assumed spherical in shape and Mie's theory was employed with the grain size distribution function being lognormal. This research is of practical significance in the design of infrared aerosols.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic Ka-band gyro-TWT with axis-encircling electrons
publicationTitle: 25th International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves (Cat. No.00EX442)
abstract: A 30 GHz second-harmonic TE/sub 21/ gyro-TWT amplifier is being constructed at UCD that will be driven by a 70 kV, 3.5 A, v/sub ⊥//v/sub Z/=1.2, Δv/sub Z//v/sub Z/=7%, axis-encircling electron beam from a Northrop Grumman cusp gun. The single-stage amplifier is predicted by a large-signal simulation code to generate 50 kW at 30 GHz with 20% efficiency, 32 dB saturated gain and 3% constant-drive bandwidth.

articleTitle: Dynamic desynchronization of BFEL optical resonator
